rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Full sequential read, chunk by chunk. Every pronoun/demonstrative (it, that, them, those, this) resolves to an antecedent in the same sentence or same paragraph within the same chunk: chunk1 L9 'It caught two more leaks' = the verifier loop, two clauses earlier; chunk2 L15 'those three modules'/'It' = 'three modules'/'The agent', one clause earlier; chunk2 L17 'it'/'them'/'the same word' = 'a word... hard-banned', named at the top of the same paragraph; chunk3 L37 'Taste closes the gap' — 'the gap' is the space just built across the whole preceding chunk3 paragraph between a rule sitting in context and the rule failing to reach the output (the chunk's own header, L29, states this explicitly), so it resolves within the same chunk, not vague. Chunk5 L49 'You have just diagnosed gaps in the M5 packaged session and mapped the work you repeat across your stack' invokes two prior module beats (exercises spot-gaps-build-the-loop and read-your-stack) — checked against the module's current include order (spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md L106: exercise spot-gaps-build-the-loop -> composing-the-workflow -> exercise read-your-stack -> the-handoff-prompt -> story-of-module-6): both beats sit earlier in the same module's deck, and this file closes the module's own arc, matching the carve-out for module-arc beats in openers/closers (also scored under rule 3 below). Arc-earned terms (M5, the loop, chat-shaped, the reference artefact, the rules file) are established within this same file at or before first callback, per the carve-out.

One candidate: chunk2 L23 'The closing lecture ended with a three-phrase benediction: "You know how to test. You know how to learn. You know how to encode."' names another file by its role (closing lecture) rather than a positional pointer, and unpacks the specific claim/quote in the same sentence — matches the rule's own PASS example shape ('the opening lecture's infinite chameleon: the LLM that flatters you...'). No other cross-file reference in body; the M5/M6 module-name callbacks are arc-earned per rule 1, not rule-2 positional pointers.

All five ## headers are true summaries of their chunk under the sequential read: 'The numbers' -> a flat numeric tally (L9); 'Things that went sideways' -> seven failure-mode paragraphs; 'A rule in context is not a rule in the output' -> the chunk states exactly this (rules loaded, still violated, 'Taste closes the gap' names the resolution) — the retitled header (see rule 17) now matches its body directly; 'Then I compounded the session' -> the prompts-run-on-the-generation + rules-moved-into-skills action; 'What the loop is for' -> the loop's rationale and the student's job. No chunk's content contradicts its own header.

Self-grading superlative: grep -niE 'one of the most|the best|nothing else|unmatched' on lines 1-60 -> 0 hits. Not-X-Not-Y-Z construction: none (chunk2 L15 'No reference artefact. No `plan.md`. No verifier.' is a flat three-item enumeration of missing artefacts, not the rule's two-negatives-then-affirmative shape, and is unchanged from the prior pin). Number+retraction: none (chunk1 counts, e.g. 'Twenty-odd', 'Ten fixes applied in all', are stated flatly, never hedged-then-restated). Abstraction-noun stacks: none (chat-shaped/the flattering end-state are concrete arc-earned terms, immediately unpacked). Verb triplets with an empty leg: none. Anaphora/epistrophe: chunk3 L31/33/35 'Everyone struggles.'/'Surprises happen.'/'The LLM is not a deterministic machine.' is three distinct short declaratives with no repeated leading phrase — not the banned anaphora shape (compare the rule's own example, which repeats 'Every session...'); chunk3 L37 'The loop caught what the subagents missed. I caught what the loop missed. You will catch what I missed.' — third leg shifts tense/addressee to the reader, the didactic point of the piece, so it carries new content, not filler.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a lecture, so headings should be claims. 'The numbers' (chunk1) is an explicitly-named accepted catalogue heading; 'Things that went sideways' (chunk2) is the same catalogue shape (a list of seven distinct anecdotes); 'Then I compounded the session' (chunk4) is a phase label inside a first-person narrative walk, also carved out; 'What the loop is for' (chunk5) is claim-adjacent (a stated purpose the content then argues). Chunk3 was previously headed 'The generalisation' — a label, not a claim, on a slide the rule's own binding clause says must carry a claim ('the claim requirement binds law and consolidation slides — where the header IS the teaching and a label would waste the beat'). It has since been retitled to '## A rule in context is not a rule in the output' (diff since pin 289b45a3), which is body text verbatim and states the chunk's consolidated claim directly. This resolves the prior non-blocking finding on this rule.
